advection_mpas.accuracy: O(h) L-inf median on a quasi-uniform Voronoi mesh (centered edge interpolation; NOT L-inf-convergent at maximally-distorted cells — see convergence fixture skip_reason)
advection_mpas.reference: Flux-form scalar advection on an MPAS C-grid (Ringler et al. 2010, J. Comput. Phys. 229:3065; Skamarock et al. 2012, Mon. Wea. Rev. 140:3090, Eq. 24 divergence of the advective flux). Pattern div($q*$u) (cf. weno5_advection's div($U*$q)): the advected tendency is the flux-form divergence of the edge flux F_e = u_e * q_hat_e, with u_e the edge-normal velocity (edge-located), q_hat_e = (q[c1]+q[c2])/2 the scalar centered-interpolated from the two flanking cells c1=cells_on_edge[1,e], c2=cells_on_edge[2,e], and (div F)_i = (1/area_cell[i]) sum_k edge_sign_on_cell[i,k]*dv_edge[e]*F_e, e=edges_on_cell[i,k]. The geometry factor edge_sign_on_cell*dv_edge/area_cell is build-time-constant (const-folded); the 1/2 weight is a literal; only the state product u_e*q_hat_e reaches the per-step hot tree. This variant binds the cell scalar as $q and the edge velocity as $u (location-guarded).

advection_mpas_velocity_first.accuracy: O(h) L-inf median on a quasi-uniform Voronoi mesh (see advection_mpas)
advection_mpas_velocity_first.reference: Operand-order MIRROR of advection_mpas: identical flux-form advection replacement, but the pattern lists the edge velocity ($u) first and the cell scalar ($q) second, so it fires for the canonical operand order where the edge-velocity variable name sorts before the cell-scalar variable name (ESS sorts commutative `*` operands by variable name). The location guards make the two variants mutually exclusive: exactly one fires for any pair of operand names. No fixtures of its own (the canonical byte contract + convergence skip live on advection_mpas); the walker SKIPs both layers for this variant.
